olivia: Heads-up — after rolling kernel-selector v2.2 to canary we see a ~12-18% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for our chat workload (mainly convo prefixes + short system prompts). Happening only on GPUs with the fused_attention path.

kevin: Can you paste the profiler traces? I want to check KV layout + whether the key hashing changed.

olivia: Minimal trace below. Root cause looks like different shard ordering in the fused kernel which changes how we compute cache keys (we were using raw tensor bytes + kv-shard-id).
```
Perf summary (canary vs baseline):
- baseline (kernel v2.1): prefix_hit 84.3%, median latency 78ms
- canary  (kernel v2.2): prefix_hit 69.1%, median latency 94ms
KV key derivation: hash(concat(model_id, shard_order, prefix_tokens))
```

sanjay: Oof. If shard_order changed deterministically between kernels, that will mutate keys for any cached prefixes. We should have canonicalized keying to be kernel-agnostic.

lara: Agreed — we had discussed normalizing by logical block index instead of physical shard id but never landed it. This is exactly the regression risk.

kevin: Repro script (quick):
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/complete -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","prompt":"conv_prefix_$(($i%20))\nuser: hello"}'
done
```
Run with baseline and canary and compare cache-hit-events counter.

l ara: small typo in script (space), but got it. Will run on a small shard farm.

perf-bot: benchmark/1812345678: run_started node-set=canary-3

perf-bot: benchmark/1812345678: run_finished prefix_hit:69.4% median_latency:95ms p95:220ms

olivia: WDYT about rolling back kernel-selector for canary until we patch keying? We can also attempt a migration step that recomputes canonical keys on first miss, but that's heavy.

kevin: Suggestion: add a transliteration layer in the runtime that maps physical shard ordering -> canonical ordering at key-creation time. Cheap and backwards-compatible. Also add a feature flag to enable legacy-key-compat mode for one week to let caches re-populate.

lara: For mitigation we can also warm caches proactively for high-volume conversation prefixes. Strategy: synthetic warmup job that plays top-1k prefixes per org. Implement as batch job hitting dedicated endpoints.

olivia: Good. A/B plan: keep canary on for 10% traffic with legacy-key-compat enabled; compare hit-rate and cost. If good, keep v2.2 with transliteration layer. If not, rollback.

kevin: I'll open a PR with transliteration patch + feature flag. Also adding unit test to assert key invariance across kernel ordering permutations.

ci-bot: PR #3872 opened by kevin: runtime: canonicalize-kv-keying + feature flag. CI: pending.

perf-bot: benchmark/1812345678: baseline-run for long-context test: prefix_hit:81.8% median_latency:120ms

lara: I'll kick off the warmup job after the transliteration job lands in staging. Also will run chat vs completion workload split: chat uses high prefix reuse; completions (stateless) shouldn't be affected.

olivia: Note for postmortem: add a short section on kernel compatibility guarantees — kernel changes must preserve any metadata we rely on for cache keys or we must derive keys from logical model schema only.

sanjay: +1. Also add a perf test that randomly shuffles shard ordering in CI to catch regressions like this.

kevin: Quick todo list: 1) PR for transliteration + flag 2) CI test for shard-order invariance 3) Warmup job script 4) A/B config for canary. I'll ping y'all when PR is green.

olivia: Thanks — ping me when A/B is live, I'll monitor token-cost and hit-rate dashboards. :mag:
